implementation_notes: Default Rust realization where the log is the broker: the group id is the durable identity and committed offsets are the retained position, bounded by topic and offset retention. Choose it when Rust services join an existing Kafka cluster.
pitfalls: Async commits can be lost on abrupt exit; use CommitMode::Sync at batch boundaries when the backlog matters.
Losing the commit position past offset retention makes the consumer resume per auto.offset.reset.

variants.name: NATS JetStream durable pull consumer with explicit ack
variants.idiom_name: async-nats jetstream durable_name pull consumer + Ack
variants.implementation_notes: Where NATS is the broker, the durable consumer's server-side state is the retained position and each message is acked explicitly, which makes the catch-up loop explicit in the code. Choose it when the stream is the integration hub and per-subscriber progress should be visible in the server.
pitfalls: Acking before the side effect loses the message; never acking causes redelivery - both are at-least-once tradeoffs.
Stream max_age and consumer inactive thresholds bound the replay window.
